title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Three false positives found by running the checks against real projects
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.2 fixes three false positives in the dead-code family, found by running it against real Android and Kotlin projects rather than trusting it. The first one gave advice that stops a module from compiling: on a 4100 file project the import check reported 222 findings, and 206 of them were this defect.

highlights.title: Imports Kotlin resolves by convention
highlights.description: import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue is required by var state by remember { … }, and the word getValue appears nowhere in the file, so the import check called it unused. Removing it on that advice fails the build with "Property delegate must have a getValue(…) method", verified with a real Gradle compile. The same held for componentN from destructuring, div behind basePath / "sub", set behind x[i] and every other operator convention. On a 4100 file project: 222 findings before, 16 after. The name list already existed and already guarded declarations, it had never been applied to imports.

highlights.title: Find Dead Islands now agrees with the member scan
highlights.description: Kotlin reads a Java getBar() as the property bar, so no call site can spell the method name. The member scan has known that since 1.42.1, the island scan did not. On a real project it reported 12 accessors, 6 of them referenced from production Kotlin, and one of those dragged a live class into an island with it.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Counts f.isBar = true as a write to a Java setBar(). A Java isX()/setX() pair becomes one Kotlin property named isX, so the setter is never written f.x = v, and it was reported as unreferenced.
The island harness takes --name=, which prints why each matching candidate is alive, with the file and line that keep it so. The outcome histogram collapsed that detail away.
